# Lerryn

> Lerryn is a self-hosted automation sandbox. Agents create Python, Node, and Shell tasks over MCP, the HTTP API, or the `lerryn` CLI; Lerryn runs them in Docker containers on the user's own machines, on schedules or webhooks, with stored credentials, logs, results, and files.

If a user asked you to install Lerryn from this site, follow the steps below. Confirm each step that changes their machine before running it.

## Install

1. Ask the user where Lerryn should run: this machine or another host, Linux or a Mac mini with OrbStack, and whether anyone besides them will reach it over the network. Docker is required.
2. Clone `https://github.com/niltavi/lerryn` on that host and follow the single-node deployment in the deployment guide: section 2 for Linux, section 2.1 for macOS with OrbStack. It uses one container with SQLite and local storage.
3. Create the administrator account before the instance is reachable by anyone else. Ask the user for the username and let them enter the password themselves; keep it out of chat and files you write.
4. Back up the master key as the guide describes, and tell the user where it is.

Before exposing the instance beyond the local network, complete the "Public deployment" section of the deployment guide.

## Connect

After the instance reports healthy, connect yourself to it as described in "Connect an agent" in the getting-started guide: remote MCP at `<public-url>/mcp` with an access token, or the stdio proxy through an authenticated `lerryn` CLI. Install the bundled Skills with `lerryn skills install`. Then run the guide's first test task to confirm that submission, execution, and result retrieval work.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://github.com/niltavi/lerryn/blob/main/docs/en/getting-started.md): connect an agent and verify a first task
- [Deployment and operations](https://github.com/niltavi/lerryn/blob/main/docs/en/deploy.md): single-node and multi-node installs, configuration, backups, upgrades, public deployment
- [CLI and MCP](https://github.com/niltavi/lerryn/blob/main/docs/en/cli.md): authentication, tasks, runs, generic API commands, Skills, and the MCP stdio proxy
- [Day-to-day operations](https://github.com/niltavi/lerryn/blob/main/docs/en/operations.md)
